speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (a) what prompted the recent inter-ministerial efforts to ban vaping; (b) how many individuals have been caught for vaping or possession offences from (i) January to June 2025 and (ii) July to August 2025; and (c) what are the Ministry's plans for the control of etomidate after its Class C classification expires on 28 February 2026.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (a) how many vaping cases have been reported via (i) hotline and (ii) webform in 2025; (b) how many of such cases led to the identification of offenders; (c) how many of these are students; and (d) whether vape use has declined since the hotline and webform were introduced.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health whether the Ministry can provide an update on the enforcement actions taken against the illegal sales of Kpods to Singapore residents through various online messaging platforms.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health what additional preventive and rehabilitative measures will be introduced to deter youth vaping and to support those already affected.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (a) how many persons have been arrested and charged with vape-related offences in the past three months; and (b) what percentage of such persons are below 25 years old; and (c) what are the recent measures by the authorities to stop the sale of e-vaporisers and components on encrypted messaging platforms.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: My response will also address written Parliamentary Questions (PQs), Question Nos 15 to 18 in today’s Order Paper, and similar questions raised by Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim1, Ms Poh Li San, Mr Sharael Taha, Dr Hamid Razak and Mr David Hoe2, scheduled for later Sittings.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I would invite Members to seek clarifications, if need be.

speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If the question has been addressed, it may not be necessary for Members to proceed with the questions for future Sittings.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: E-vaporisers, which were primarily nicotine delivery devices, were banned in Singapore ever since it was introduced.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: However, e-vaporisers now carry more dangerous substances, like etomidate, and controlled drugs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The HSA, Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA), Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB) and Singapore Police Force (SPF) work closely to enforce against smuggling and syndicated activities at our borders.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They are also sharing information with their foreign counterparts.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Within the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) today, Singapore, Brunei, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia have banned vaping.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are pleased to learn that Malaysia is making plans to do so too.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: With more regional countries banning e-vaporisers, we can be more effective in curbing this harmful and addictive habit.
This has sent a clear and strong public message, by elevating the penalties against etomidate-related offences.
Together with this, we now have over 10,000 officers empowered to enforce against e-vaporiser-related offences.
Agencies have been conducting joint raids at night spots and operations at Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs).
Public vigilance continues to be crucial in enabling offences to be detected.
The online form requires Singpass login to prevent spam and ensure report integrity, especially if the reporting member of public wants to upload photos of offenders or locations of offence.
For those without Singpass, such as those under 15 years old, they can use the telephone hotline.
Because of our strong stance against substance abuse, it is unlikely that production of etomidate e-vaporisers will take root in Singapore.

As for the question of phasing out etomidate in medical settings, etomidate remains a useful anaesthetic agent, particularly in emergencies for intubation purposes and we have no plans to phase it out.
Its handling has been well-controlled, previously under the Poisons Act and now under the MDA.
I mentioned earlier that e-vaporisers have changed the landscape of substance abuse.
There are more young people involved, out of curiosity, or succumbing to peer pressure.
We want to help this group and have provided opportunities for them to come forward and seek help early.
These devices have been properly disposed of; no testing was done of their contents because that will take up a lot of our testing resources. "Bin the Vape" was meant to be a time-limited initiative.
We have since reduced the number of bins and located them in specific locations, such as border checkpoints and where rehabilitation programmes are provided.
Second, we introduced or stepped up rehabilitation programmes, namely the QuitVape and I Quit programmes, to support users to kick the habit.
Those who voluntarily surrender e-vaporisers, including etomidate e-vaporisers and seek help, will not be penalised for doing so.
This arrangement has continued since 1 September 2025.
But as for those who are caught, rehabilitation will be required for all etomidate e-vaporiser offenders and repeat e-vaporiser offenders.

The rehabilitation programmes are run by the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) and social service agencies (SSAs), such as, WE CARE Community Services and the Singapore Anti-Narcotics Association (SANA) who have expertise in running cessation programmes.
Schools and parents are closely involved in the rehabilitation process for youths, including counselling and supporting the youths.
We also need to step up preventive education.
Schools and IHLs are intensifying educational efforts through school curricula, assembly talks and orientation briefings.
Students learn about the harms of vaping, recognise impulsive and addictive behaviours and pick up strategies for self-control, help-seeking and managing negative peer influences.
The Ministry of Education (MOE) is also engaging parents, including through the Parents Gateway.
While we have listed etomidate in the MDA, the Ministry of Health (MOH) is reviewing the longer-term legislation needed to adapt to this new landscape.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: In this House, I have asked many PQs about vaping since 2021.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: How many vaping equipment and vaping materials have been surrendered through the "bins" and through voluntary purposes since they started programme?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: And secondly, how many people have come voluntarily to HSA for help, because they have already surrendered their vaping equipment and need rehabilitation?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: And third question, is, moving on, which Ministry or department will continue the effort against vaping?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I noted that the recent HSA's annual report, in the front page, report by the Chairman, there is no mention about vaping, as I mentioned the last round in my supplementary question previously.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: More have been surrendered earlier but we did not keep track of them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for volunteers who gave up vapes since we announced the new policies, 74 have come forward, as I mentioned in my reply.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Which Ministry will coordinate between the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and MOH, we will work closely together to coordinate.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It used to be either you smoke and vape, or you take drugs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But now you have a vape device, it is a delivery device that contains the drugs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The front end is controlled by MOH, controlled substance is regulated by MHA.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The two Ministries have to work closely together and coordinate this.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: According to news reports, these youths are enticed to vaping and peddling of vapes through social media channels.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think the challenge is not one of resource, but through the Internet and messaging platforms, they proliferate very easily and they do not necessarily have a presence in Singapore for you to able to get hold of them and take them to task.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, it is a big cat and mouse game.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have shut down so many of them – I reported it in my reply – and working together with the Info-communications Media Development Authority (IMDA), as well as the tech platforms.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But most importantly, the culture of avoiding substance abuse must take root in our society.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: What has been very comforting is that ever since we launched this new whole-of-Government approach to tackling etomidate vaping, the public has been very supportive.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Schools, institutions, SSAs and even the youths amongst themselves are very supportive.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, we hope we continue to uphold this behaviour and this culture, and I think that is the best defence against substance abuse.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I am trying to see those who have asked PQs earlier, I will give priority.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If there are not, I will go to the rest.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: In view of the tightened measures to eradicate the use of vapes in Singapore, this has also caused a shift to more underground activities.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: What are the Government's measures to target this group of sales of vapes, especially Kpods, in underground activities?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Never think that just because we are worried about underground activities, so therefore, legalise and regulate.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That is what other countries have done when it comes to controlled drugs; and look where they are, and look where we are.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, I think we have always taken a tough stance against drugs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I do not know why I am answering this, but I think it is a correct approach to take.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Do not fall for harm reduction arguments, ban it, enforce it; if it goes underground, we will go after you.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I understand that I did not file a PQ on this, but I am just wondering if the enhanced stance against vaping will now, in fact, empower the SPF and not just the HSA, to apprehend individuals reported to be using or distributing vapes?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I ask because the previous appeals I had written on behalf of residents to the SPF had been redirected.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The concern however, in doing so, is two-fold.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The presence of HSA officers, presumably is not as ubiquitous as that of the Police and HSA may not potentially have sufficient resources to tackle the surge in cases.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This is something that Member Melvin Yong had also raised previously.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Perhaps it is not within your Ministry, Sir, but I am wondering if we could have your thoughts on that.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I just like to re-introduce the subutex experience all those years ago.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I remember we had to fill the gap with subutex and it took some time to fill the gap for subutex before we could classify it as an illegal drug and then take enforcement action.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I just see a little bit of similarity here with etomidate.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I am concerned at the length of time it took HSA to classify this as a Class C drug.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I do not know the ins and outs of HSA.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There could be a number of reasons why the experiments had to take so long or the policy considerations.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Because only then, can you come in and do all the enforcement.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The classification of etomidate under MDA is done under MHA.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have to act as fast as we can.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The process does take some time when the new substance enters a community.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: You have to observe who is taking it, will it fizzle out or will it start to take root and grow.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: At the same time, we have to observe the clinical evidence.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, all these take a bit of time.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have to act as quickly as we can.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: There is a case in my division, where the child is hooked on Kpods and expelled from school.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: His parents want to know what powers do the authorities have to enforce compulsory assessment and rehabilitation for these youths that refuse our help?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One is echoing from what Parliamentary colleague, Mr Christopher de Souza has said, I would like to ask whether, apart from the etomidate-laced vapes, has the Ministry detected the use of other unlawful or harmful substances as well, that may potentially be also classified?
The other supplementary question is pertaining to MOE's recent announcements on introducing suspensions.

In this regard, I would like to inquire whether we are exploring for these suspensions to be in-house, which means it is within the school, rather than external, as an effort to rehabilitate the students better.
This is following from some of the feedback that we have gathered through Woodgrove's anti-vaping taskforce through which we have been engaging the schools.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On the first question, I assume the Member is asking whether there are other substances that are delivered through e-vaporisers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have seen them in other countries – cannabis, for example; in Australia, we saw fentanyl.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, we have to observe this carefully and, as Mr de Souza mentioned, be very vigilant, list them quickly, do not allow them to take root.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for the next question, about MOE, I think I will answer on behalf of MOE, their measures are over and above what the law has provided.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Would it be possible to include etomidate's precursors under the precursors control list?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But if we have missed out something, do let us know and we will include them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The second question, I think we just have to be tough on all forms of substance abuse so that one does not become the substitute of the other.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is an area where MHA will obviously know a lot better.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But right now, as I have mentioned, e-vaporisers have changed the landscape.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Now, you have got something very recreational, a delivery device – from delivering lychee-flavoured nicotine, to etomidate to cannabis.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, you have a range of stuff that can be delivered through this device.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When someone is using a vape, you do not know what he or she is consuming.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Because of that, MHA and MOH will have to work closely together, so that we cover all bases.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, whatever substance abuse is out there, we take firm action against them, so that one does not become a substitute for the other.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have had some informal consultations and we hope ASEAN, at some point, can take a concerted stance.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is something that we want to work towards.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In the meantime, we do see more and more ASEAN countries banning vapes, Malaysia being the latest to attempt to do so, and we will share our information and our experiences with them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Hopefully, at some point, we will have a stronger ASEAN common stance.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Minister, to the extent that smoking is precursor to vaping and with the clampdown on vaping, does the Ministry intend to take a tighter stance against smoking, especially among our young?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The good thing is that smoking prevalence has been dropping in Singapore continuously.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will continue to encourage people not to smoke.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We should also remember that tobacco has been around for 200 years.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When it first started, people did not know the harm that it can cause.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Today, we know but it has taken root and become part of society's behaviour.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we will have to continue to work on reducing the prevalence of smoking.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We have many PQs in this list, so I am going to give this one last supplementary question to Dr Wan Rizal.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Minister, you mentioned the involvement of IMH in these efforts to reduce our vaping issues.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We clearly know IMH is very much involved with rehabilitation and cessation programmes too.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: With this expansion, how will it affect IMH's operational ability, given that we do have many cases of mental health also requiring attention?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And especially since we see a surge in youth numbers coming forward, which is a good thing, but it also affects the system.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: IMH does a lot of things, with different departments.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, the department for cessation, which is called National Addictions Management Service (NAMS), have their dedicated resources.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, they will not be using resources that are used to treat or to help mental illness cases.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That said, we are just starting our operations.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If there is a need for more resources, we will beef them up.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As for youths, we are working closely with the Ministry of Social and Family Development and the SSAs, such as WeCare and Fei Yue, who have experience working with youths.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They are already starting operations on cessation programmes for youths.
